test_title: PYST 28: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 17 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which enzyme, secreted by the chief cells of the stomach, is crucial for initiating the digestion of proteins?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pepsinogen (converted to pepsin)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pepsinogen** is secreted by the chief cells of the stomach and is an inactive precursor enzyme (zymogen).
 
• It is converted into its active form, **pepsin**, in the presence of hydrochloric acid (HCl) secreted by the parietal cells.
 
• **Pepsin** is the primary enzyme responsible for breaking down proteins into smaller peptides in the acidic environment of the stomach.
 
• The activation of pepsinogen ensures that protein digestion begins in the stomach, which is essential for nutrient absorption in later stages of digestion.
 
• The stomach’s acidic pH (approximately 1.5–3.5) is crucial for the activation and function of pepsin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Cells:** Specialized cells located in the stomach lining that produce pepsinogen and gastric lipase.
 
• **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl):** Secreted by parietal cells in the stomach, HCl lowers the pH and facilitates the activation of pepsinogen into pepsin.
 
• **Protein Digestion:** Proteins are broken into smaller peptides by pepsin, and later into amino acids by enzymes in the small intestine like trypsin and chymotrypsin.
 
• **Trypsinogen vs. Pepsinogen:** Trypsinogen is secreted by the pancreas and activated into trypsin in the small intestine, while pepsinogen is activated into pepsin in the stomach.
 
• **Zymogen Activation:** Zymogens like pepsinogen are inactive forms of enzymes, activated under specific conditions to prevent self-digestion of the tissue that produces them.
